text:
alex: Heads-up — I'm about to open a PR for a dependency-gardening refactor across billing/, creds/ and network/ TF modules. Goal: centralize provider blocks in the root module, standardize provider aliases, and normalize secret paths to `secret/data/redwood/...` so k8s secret names and KMS keys line up. Planning a staging canary after PR.

priya: +1. couple quick q's: are you planning to regenerate terraform.lock.hcl in each module or keep a single canonical lockfile at the repo root? lockfile churn is the main pain in previous rollouts.

alex: Prefer single canonical lockfile at repo root. We keep module sources pinned (registry or git tag) but run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` from repo root to produce one lockfile. Only update if provider versions actually change. Will include a note in the PR about why_lockfile_should_change.md :eyes:

jordan: FYI k8s manifests depend on the secret name pattern. If secret path changes, deployment tooling (helm values + infra service) expects `redwood-<env>-creds`. Need a migration plan so staging and prod don't diverge.

morgan: Also watch provider aliasing. If we hoist providers and add aliases we must update module inputs that expect `provider = aws.some` vs implicit provider. Otherwise TF plan will want to replace resources. Suggest adding a compatibility shim: keep old aliases for one release, then remove.

alex: Good call. Draft checklist in the PR description will include:
- hoist provider blocks to root & add aliased fallbacks
- run `terraform init && terraform plan -target=module.billing -out=canary.plan` in staging
- run `scripts/secretname-mapping.sh staging` to preview k8s secret renames
- regeneration of root terraform.lock.hcl only when `terraform providers mirror` shows changes
- compatibility rollback steps (recreate alias mapping)

priya: I'll add a CI job `tf-dep-compat-check` to run `terraform init && terraform validate && terraform plan -lock=false -out=ci.plan` for affected modules and diff the plan to a golden plan. If lockfile changes we fail and require manual ack.

jordan: For the k8s side, I can wire a post-merge migration that creates duplicate secret names in staging (old and new) for 48h, so controllers don't flip. Quick sed for helm values:
```
# preview change
git grep -n "redwood-[a-z]\+-creds" | xargs -I{} sed -n '1,3p' {}
# to update
sed -i 's/redwood-\([a-z]\+\)-creds/redwood-\1-creds-v2/g' charts/**/values.yaml
```

morgan: If you run `terraform state mv` for affected resources remember to coordinate with release window (state lock). Also add a smoke test that queries secrets via KMS to ensure decryption path intact.

alex: I'll coordinate a 30-minute window for the state moves and add the smoke tests to the canary run. PR will include the alias shim and explicit `provider` param updates per module, plus migration docs. @priya can you add the CI job and a lockfile diff gate? @jordan can you prepare the helm migration script? @morgan can you draft the state-move runbook?

priya: Yep I got this. I'll put a small GH Action that runs against a PR branch and posts `ci/terraform-compat: pass/fail` as a comment.

jordan: Preparing helm script now, will drop it in `infra/tools/helm-migrate/` and link it in the PR. I'll also include a preview command for owners to run locally.

morgan: Will draft state-move runbook and a checklist for oncall handoff. Will add KMS smoke test to `infra/tests/smoke/secret-decrypt.test.sh`.

infra-bot: CI: terraform-plan (staging-canary) succeeded for branch alex/dep-garden - job #324 — artifacts: canary.plan

alex: Nice, thanks all. I'll open the PR in ~30m and tag reviewers. Quick ask: when reviewing, focus on provider alias fallbacks and the lockfile diff only — other cosmetic changes can be a follow-up. :thumbsup:

priya: Roger that. I'll gate the lockfile diff and add a small blurb about regenerating lockfile in the contributors guide.

jordan: I'll review helm changes quickly once PR is up. :eyes:

morgan: Ready to be on-call for the state move window. Ping me in #eng-oncall when we pick the time.

alex: Will do. Thanks everyone!
